correctness.rationale: In units of R=v/κ the independent thermal OU term has variance ν=Dκ/v². For U=y² and t=1/(2ν), integration of the derivative of u^(j+1/2)(1−u)^ℓ exp(−tu) gives the stated tilted moment recurrence, with both boundary terms zero. The central curvature has the sign of F=2t E_t[U]−1. At a zero the recurrence gives E_t[U²]=(2ℓ+1)ν², so F'=(1−ℓ)/t. F(0)=−1 and the small-u Laplace expansion gives F(t)=(1−ℓ)/t+O(t^−2) at large t. Every zero crosses upward, so there is exactly one. Gaussian differentiation and the next moment give P⁽⁴⁾/P=2(ℓ−1)/ν_c² and P⁽⁶⁾/P=2(ℓ−1)[1+(2ℓ−9)ν_c]/ν_c⁴. In the even analytic equation P'/z=0, put B=P⁽⁴⁾/6 and C=P⁽⁶⁾/120 at criticality. The heat equation gives coefficients −3Bδ+15Cδ² in the constant term and B−10Cδ in the term linear in z². The implicit solution is z²=3δ+(6C/B)δ²+O_ℓ(δ³); 6C/B is exactly the claimed K. These stationary points are maxima since B<0. For the global mode count, cap the beta density at a finite height on [−1,1]. Its distributional derivative has, in order, positive edge jump, negative slope, positive slope, negative edge jump. Gaussian variation diminution bounds the number of sign changes by three; L¹ convergence of the capped densities gives uniform convergence of the convolved derivatives and preserves that bound. Oddness, the sign near zero (controlled at criticality by P⁽⁴⁾<0), and negative derivative for z>1 give exactly two peaks below and one at or above threshold. Finally, weak convergence to the two endpoint atoms gives F→2t−1 at fixed t and brackets ν_c→1; convergence to the uniform density gives limiting curvature G_ν'(1)<0 at each fixed ν>0 and hence ν_c→0. The limits of K are −12/5 and +∞. The strict curvature crossing yields continuous ν_c and K, giving existence, not uniqueness, of an intermediate zero. Multiplying by R² and using δ=κ(D_c−D)/v² gives the stated dimensional factors.
residual_risks: The independent numerical check corroborates the proof and does not certify a remainder or uniformity. The expansion is for fixed 0<ℓ<1 with fixed physical trap and propulsion parameters; the endpoint limits concern K alone.
